title: Anna Christie at St Ann’s Warehouse #annachristie #michellewilliams #...
transcript: Head to Brooklyn to see Michelle Williams on a barge with daddy issues and a troubled past — just don't expect much to actually happen. A young woman named Anna reunites with her estranged father, falls for a sailor, and struggles to find herself. The whole thing is very slow, which I suppose isn't inherently a problem. The problem is that the flow of information is just as slow as the action, as if you could zone out for five minutes and not miss anything. The play itself also feels dated, and it's not clear to me why you'd want to produce it in 2025, unless you have someone perfect in mind for the lead role, which Michelle Williams is not. I thought her performance was fine, but her accent was all over the place. She also doesn't reach the same level of emotional intensity as her luminous co stars Tom Sturridge and Brian d'Arcy James, so there are parts of the play where it feels like she's not in the same world with them. But really, my biggest issue here was the play itself. Act 1 was a slog and Act 2 was stronger, but still kept spinning its wheels a lot, and I thought the whole thing could have been like 20 minutes shorter. The sluggishness is exacerbated by the fact that for such a bare set, there's a lot of tedious busy work in the scene transitions — stunning lighting design, though. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer criticizes nearly every major element — slow pacing, dated material, miscast lead, inconsistent accent, tedious transitions — with only lighting and supporting performances praised. The overall verdict is clearly discouraging.
